#--------------------------------------------- \# Topic Modeling: pilot sample #---------------------------------------------

### Import Data


#rsw comment - it would be useful to understand how you categorized as article as focal or not. a sentence or two explaining that method would be good.


```{r}
# import 806 articles (Nexis Uni full text + screening labels)
articles <- read_csv(here::here("806_articles_fulltext.csv"))

# keep the 700-article probability sample
sample700 <- articles %>% 
  filter(in700 == TRUE)

# subset the 40 relevant (focal) articles
relevant <- sample700 %>% 
  filter(focal == TRUE)

# subset the 660 irrelevant articles
irrelevant <- sample700 %>% 
  filter(focal == FALSE)

#quick check
nrow(sample700)    # should be 700
nrow(relevant)     # should be 40
nrow(irrelevant)   # should be 660
count(sample700, period, focal)
```

# Topic Modeling all 700 articles

### Process into corpus object

```{r}
textdata <- sample700 %>% 
  select(doc_id, text, year, period, focal) %>% 
  as.data.frame()
```

### Remove stopwords, clean corpus

```{r}
# 1. Standard stopwords plus common news words
english_stopwords <- c(stopwords("en"), 
                       "said", "says", "also", "can", "will", "one", "new", "like", "just")

# 2. Build corpus
corpus <- Corpus(DataframeSource(textdata))

# 3. Clean in correct sequence
processedCorpus <- tm_map(corpus, content_transformer(tolower))
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, removePunctuation, preserve_intra_word_dashes = TRUE)
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, removeNumbers)


# Remove stopwords BEFORE stemming
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, removeWords, english_stopwords)

# Stem documents after removing stopwords
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, stemDocument, language = "en")
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, stripWhitespace)
```

```{r tm3a}
#DTM: rows correspond to the documents in the corpus. Columns correspond to the terms in the documents. Cells correspond to the weights of the terms. (Girder)
# compute document term matrix with terms >= minimumFrequency
minimumFrequency <- 5
DTM <- DocumentTermMatrix(processedCorpus, control = list(bounds = list(global = c(minimumFrequency, Inf))))

# have a look at the number of documents and terms in the matrix
dim(DTM)
# due to vocabulary pruning, we have empty rows in our DTM
# LDA does not like this. So we remove those docs from the
# DTM and the metadata
sel_idx <- slam::row_sums(DTM) > 0
DTM <- DTM[sel_idx, ]
textdata <- textdata[sel_idx, ]
dim(DTM)

```

## Topic proportions over time {.unnumbered}

```{r}
# append period labels for aggregation (in time order)
textdata$period_label <- factor(textdata$period,
                                levels = c("P1", "P2", "P3", "P4"),
                                labels = c("2022.12-2023", "2024", "2025", "2026.1-2026.9"))
```

Articles per period

```{r}
articles_periods <- textdata %>% 
  distinct(doc_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  count(period_label) %>% 
  mutate(pct_total = (n/sum(n))) %>% 
  mutate(pct_total = formattable::percent(pct_total)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(period_label))

articles_periods %>%
  kbl(caption = "Pilot Sample Articles by Period (n=699, 11/14/2026)", font_size = 30) %>%
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria") %>% 
  column_spec(1, bold = T, border_right = T) %>%
  column_spec(2, width = "5em") %>% 
  column_spec(3, width = "5em", background = "yellow") 

#Fact check 699 articles
#sum(articles_periods$n) # yes, it is 699
```

```{r tm12}
# number of topics
K <- 6
# set random number generator seed
set.seed(9161)
#Latent Dirichlet Allocation, LDA
topicModel2 <- LDA(DTM, K, method="Gibbs", control=list(iter = 500, verbose = 25, alpha = 0.2))
tmResult <- posterior(topicModel2)
theta <- tmResult$topics
beta <- tmResult$terms
topicNames <- apply(terms(topicModel2, 10), 2, paste, collapse = " ")  # reset topicnames
```

### Mean topic proportions per period

```{r}
# Step 1: Check dimensions
n_theta <- nrow(theta)
n_textdata <- length(textdata$period_label)

cat("Number of rows in theta: ", n_theta, "\n")
cat("Number of documents in textdata: ", n_textdata, "\n")

# Check if textdata contains all the documents in theta
common_ids <- intersect(rownames(theta), textdata$doc_id)

# Filter textdata to include only the documents present in theta
textdata_filtered <- textdata[textdata$doc_id %in% common_ids, ]

# Check dimensions after filtering
n_textdata_filtered <- nrow(textdata_filtered)
cat("Number of documents in filtered textdata: ", n_textdata_filtered, "\n")

# Ensure the lengths match now
if (n_theta != n_textdata_filtered) {
  stop("The number of rows in 'theta' still does not match the length of 'textdata_filtered$period_label'.")
}

# Align rownames of theta with filtered textdata
theta_aligned <- theta[rownames(theta) %in% textdata_filtered$doc_id, ]

# Optional: Verify the order of documents
if (!all(rownames(theta_aligned) == textdata_filtered$doc_id)) {
  # If the order doesn't match, reorder one to match the other
  textdata_filtered <- textdata_filtered[match(rownames(theta_aligned), textdata_filtered$doc_id), ]
}

# Ensure they are now aligned and can be combined
if (!all(rownames(theta_aligned) == textdata_filtered$doc_id)) {
  stop("The document IDs still do not match. Please check the data alignment.")
}

# Step 2: Combine data
topic_data <- data.frame(theta_aligned, period_label = textdata_filtered$period_label)

# Step 3: Aggregate data
topic_proportion_per_period <- aggregate(. ~ period_label, data = topic_data, FUN = mean)

# set topic names to aggregated columns
colnames(topic_proportion_per_period)[2:(K+1)] <- topicNames
# reshape data frame
vizDataFrame <- melt(topic_proportion_per_period, id.vars = "period_label")
```

topics

### Review the topics and determine a 1-2 word label after reading the source documents.

The function below lists the 20 articles that load most on a topic, with headline, outlet, and whether the article is relevant (focal = TRUE).

```{r}
top_articles_for <- function(topic_n) {
  as.data.frame(theta) %>% 
    rownames_to_column(var = "doc_id") %>% 
    rename(topic = all_of(as.character(topic_n))) %>% 
    top_n(20, topic) %>% 
    arrange(desc(topic)) %>% 
    left_join(sample700 %>% select(doc_id, focal, headline, outlet), by = "doc_id") %>% 
    select(doc_id, focal, headline, outlet, topic)
}
```

# Relevant and Irrelevant Topics

Mean topic proportion in relevant articles (lay use of GenAI chatbots for health is the central subject) and irrelevant articles. A topic with a much higher share in relevant articles is a relevant topic.

```{r}
# number of relevant and irrelevant articles in the model
table(textdata$focal)

# mean topic proportion by group
topic_by_focal <- aggregate(theta, by = list(focal = textdata$focal), mean)
colnames(topic_by_focal)[2:(K+1)] <- topic_labels

# table: one row per topic
relevance_table <- topic_by_focal %>% 
  pivot_longer(-focal, names_to = "topic", values_to = "mean_proportion") %>% 
  mutate(focal = if_else(focal, "relevant", "irrelevant")) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = focal, values_from = mean_proportion) %>% 
  mutate(difference = relevant - irrelevant) %>% 
  arrange(desc(difference))

relevance_table %>%
  kbl(caption = "Mean Topic Proportion in Relevant vs. Irrelevant Articles", digits = 3) %>%
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria")
```

#Figure: Relevant vs. irrelevant topics

```{r}
relevance_table %>% 
  pivot_longer(c(relevant, irrelevant), names_to = "group", values_to = "mean_proportion") %>% 
  mutate(topic = fct_reorder(topic, difference)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_proportion, y = topic, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("relevant" = "lightblue", "irrelevant" = "lightpink"), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Which Topics Do Relevant Articles Use?",
       subtitle = "Relevant = lay use of GenAI chatbots for health is the central subject",
       x = "mean topic proportion", y = NULL,
       caption = "Pilot sample, n=699. Graphic by Zirong Li, 11-15-2026")
```

# Summary

I ran an LDA topic model (K = 6) on the 699 articles in my Pilot sample, drawn from a broad AI-and-health search in Nexis Uni. Only 40 of them are relevant to my project after screening: lay people’s use of GenAI chatbots for health is the central subject. I compared each topic’s average share in the relevant and irrelevant articles.

One topic is clearly relevant. Chatbot use and risks makes up 42% of the relevant articles but 17% of the others. Its top articles cover ChatGPT and teen mental health, a California law on companion chatbots, and lawsuits against OpenAI, the same harm stories I found when reading the full articles. Medical AI is partly relevant (22% vs. 15%), but it covers clinical tools for doctors, not lay users. Four topics are irrelevant: business and markets, tech products, politics, and lifestyle and entertainment (horoscopes, recipes, reviews), most of which never mention generative AI.

The benefit is a quick map of a large sample. The model shows where the noise in my search comes from, which will help me revise the search string before collecting the full corpus. The shortfalls are clear. The chatbot topic mixes health stories with campus stories about AI and cheating as an example, so it does not show the rise in relevant coverage from 2023 to 2026 that I found by reading. Some relevant articles fall into unrelated topics. Topics are word patterns, not frames. They cannot show the roles, attribution, or advice my research questions ask about, so I still need the codebook.
